name: Qdrant
model: Collections of points: dense or sparse vectors plus a JSON payload; filtered similarity and hybrid search over REST and gRPC
engine_note: Rust; HNSW per segment, modified so payload filters are checked during graph search; WAL plus segments on local disk, vectors in RAM or memory-mapped
consistency: Single-point operations; no multi-point transactions. Write goes to a WAL first (survives power loss). Replicated clusters favour availability: write_consistency_factor 1, read consistency 1 and weak write ordering by default, so replica reads can be stale; stricter is optional.
scaling: Horizontal: collections split into shards (consistent hashing by default, or user-defined, e.g. per tenant) with replicas; Raft keeps cluster topology; resharding only in Qdrant Cloud.
managed: Qdrant Hybrid Cloud (your Kubernetes, Qdrant-run control plane)
reach: Reach for it for a dedicated vector store where most searches carry filters (tenant, language, date) and you want them fast and accurate.
avoid: Avoid if you need transactions across vectors and business rows, or the vector count is small enough for pgvector in the Postgres you already run.
escape: It filters inside the vector index and scales vectors beyond what a single Postgres with pgvector holds comfortably.
chat: Message embeddings with user_id and chat_id in the payload, searched with a user filter.
notes: CLAIM CHECK (b) 'Qdrant evaluates the filter during graph traversal rather than before or after it': VERIFIED, with a nuance. Article 'Filtrable HNSW' (2019-11-24, https://qdrant.tech/articles/filterable-hnsw/): 'What if we simply apply the filter criteria to the nodes of this graph and use in the greedy search only those that meet these criteria?' and it adds edges so filtered subgraphs stay connected: 'we can guarantee that the HNSW graph will be connected simply by creating additional edges inside each category separately'. Indexing docs (https://qdrant.tech/documentation/concepts/indexing/): 'HNSW is well-compatible with the modification that allows Qdrant to use filters during a search.' Nuance: a query planner may skip the graph; docs: 'When the maximum estimated amount of points that a condition satisfies is smaller than full_scan_threshold_kb, the query planner will use full-scan search instead of HNSW index traversal' (payload index used to estimate cardinality). So for very selective filters it is effectively filter-first. Consistency quotes: 'The write_consistency_factor ... It is set to 1 by default.'; 'default consistency is 1'; 'weak (default) ordering does not provide any additional guarantees, so write operations can be freely reordered.'; 'a point may already be visible on one replica but not yet on another.' WAL quote: 'Once a change has been added to the WAL, it will not be lost even if a power loss occurs.' Resharding quote: 'resharding is only available in Qdrant Cloud and otherwise requires recreating the collection'. No Jepsen analysis.
